text:
This was my first time using the government-subsidized dental clinic.
When I entered the examination room, the doctor didn't even look at my teeth. He just asked which tooth needed filling.
He didn't ask about any symptoms at all.
I thought to myself, "I'm not a doctor, how would I know?" When I opened my mouth, I told him my teeth had been feeling sensitive for 2-3 days. He couldn't find anything and said we needed an X-ray, which I understand.
Then it was time for the filling. He just lightly filled the tooth, then I heard a machine beep and he told me to clench my teeth. After that, I rinsed my mouth (it was very quick, in my opinion).
Before leaving the room, the doctor gave me some advice.
He said what to do if my teeth become sensitive again. This part wasn't a problem.
(But I was very bothered by the filling process itself.) Other than that, the service was good.

The dentist was very heavy-handed; scraping the tartar was very painful. They did it quite forcefully. It was over quickly, but it hurt. There was also a 2-hour wait, even though I had booked an appointment in advance.
The counter staff were polite and provided good service, and the dentist and assistant were also friendly.
